newsitem.title: USA: Revoke Arafat's Nobel Prize, says Wiesenthal Center.
newsitem.headline: Revoke Arafat's Nobel Prize, says Wiesenthal Center.

text.p: The Simon Wiesenthal Centre called on Thursday for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to be stripped of his Nobel Peace Prize because of the recent murders of Palestinians who sold land to Jews.

The policy of Arafat's Palestinian Authority "to issue a death sentence to anyone engaged in selling Palestinian land to a Jew...makes a mockery of the Nobel Peace Prize," Rabbi Marvin Hier said in a statement.
Hier, founder and dean of the Simon Wiesenthal Centre, wrote to Nobel Committee Chairman Francis Sejerstedt in Norway asking that Arafat's 1994 prize be revoked.
He noted three Arabs had been "executed without trial" since Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen was quoted on May 4 as saying Palestinians who sold land to Jews faced execution.
Hier said the "death sentence" decision was approved by Arafat.

"Sanctioning the murder without trial of individuals accused of selling land to Jews not only violates the letter and spirit of the Oslo Accords, but is a form of behaviour reminiscent of the Dark Ages and reeks of the anti-Semitism invoked by the Nazis through their infamous Nuremberg Laws," his statement said.

"Your committee...which had the courage to praise Mr Arafat for seeking reconciliation and peace with Israel, must now have the same courage to condemn him for besmirching the high honour you have bestowed on him by rescinding the award," Hier wrote to Sejerstedt.
He said the Simon Wiesenthal Centre was calling on human rights organisations and "advocates of democracy" everywhere to join an international campaign to have Arafat's Nobel Prize revoked.
